correctness.summary: The Gegenbauer product formula for every real lambda>0 yields a normalized hypergroup convolution whose cap self-convolution can be evaluated explicitly by a two-variable linear change of coordinates. The resulting profile is (cos beta)^(2 lambda)/pi times the integral of (tan^2 beta-tan^2 u)^lambda. Its nth Gegenbauer coefficient is the square of the cap coefficient and is positive except at finitely many beta values. Lu's full-support positive-mixture lemmas transfer this strict coefficient positivity to the truncated-power profile (t-r)_+^(lambda+1), including t=pi via a separate completely-monotone representation. Positive beta convolution then gives every delta>lambda+1.

originality.scope: to the best of our knowledge
originality.summary: Beatson--zu Castell--Xu state Conjecture 1.4 for arbitrary real lambda>0 and explicitly say this is greater generality than required for their sphere application. Xu's 2018 Jacobi theorem is stated for alpha,beta in N_0; Lu's 2025 truncated-power theorem is stated on ordinary integer-dimensional spheres, so the spectral Gegenbauer parameter remains discrete. Beatson--zu Castell's 2017 convolution theory does allow arbitrary lambda>0 but does not state the all-real Polya boundary theorem. Targeted searches found no source asserting the continuous-real-parameter conclusion. Later descriptions that 'the conjecture' was proved appear to refer to the sphere-relevant discrete cases, so the novelty claim is restricted to the continuous-parameter sufficiency extension.

value.summary: The result proves the sufficiency half of the literal all-real parameter range in a published conjecture and identifies a reusable continuous-parameter cap-convolution identity. The normalized identity exactly interpolates the usual spherical-cap intersection formula and lets positive-mixture methods move from integer dimensions to the full Gegenbauer hypergroup.

limitations: The necessity direction delta<lambda+1 is not proved.
The new claim is the continuous real Gegenbauer-parameter extension, not new integer-dimensional sphere cases.
The proof imports Lu's positive-mixture lemmas rather than reproving their complete-monotonicity calculations.
A differently formulated or poorly indexed equivalent result may exist.
Independent audit has not been performed.
